newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1997 car market to grow to 2 mln units -- CSP.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1997 car market to grow to 2 mln units -- CSP.

text.p: The Italian car market is seen growing to over two million vehicles in 1997 from 1.73 million in 1996 helped by the government's car-buying incentive scheme, said researcher group Centro Studi Promotor (CSP).

For January, CSP expects Italian car sales to rise to 255,000, up 33 percent over January 1996, and it sees the increases continuing in the following months. The Ministry of Transport to set to release January new car data on February 10.
CSP forecast that 44 percent of the new orders will benefit from the incentive scheme, with the majority of these cars purchased being in the small car category.
Around half of the orders for small cars will come due to the incentive scheme while a third of sales of medium to larger cars will gain from the buying scheme, it added.
Italy introduced its car buying scheme in early January, offering incentives for car owners who trade in cars over 10 years old to buy new models.
